pageCache.pageTitle: Our Values - Hook Lane Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our Values
text
At Hook Lane Primary School, our values are much more than words on a wall. We have adopted a set of Learner Qualities that we believe are the essential ingredients for success, not only at school but throughout life.
These qualities underpin everything we do, helping our children to become confident, curious, resilient and independent learners who are ready to embrace new opportunities and challenges. They are at the heart of our school motto, Encouraging Fearless Learners, reflecting our commitment to developing children who are willing to take risks, embrace mistakes, and grow through every experience.
To ensure these values are truly embedded in our school community, we have also named each of our classes after one of our Learner Qualities. Every child belongs to a class that celebrates an important characteristic of successful learning, reminding them every day of the attitudes and behaviours that will help them thrive.
Our Learner Qualities are:
Create, Captivate, Wonder, Explore, Strive, Reflect, Persevere, Challenge, Motivate, Achieve, Discover, Resilience, Imagine, Fearless, Mastery and Fortitude.
Together, these qualities inspire our children to be ambitious, lifelong learners who approach the world with curiosity, determination and confidence. By living these values every day, we are truly Encouraging Fearless Learners.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher Welcome - Hook Lane Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher Welcome
welcome
Welcome to Hook Lane Primary School,
Our motto is Encouraging Fearless Learners.
We achieve this through a broad, varied and engaging curriculum, delivered in an environment where children feel both safe and challenged. At Hook Lane, we build a culture rooted in kindness, respect and high expectations, where happy children and happy staff are able to thrive and achieve.
We are committed to ensuring that every child makes strong progress from their individual starting point. We recognise that all learners are different, and we support each child to develop confidence, resilience and a love of learning that will stay with them for life.
Our teaching encourages curiosity, active participation and deep understanding. We model challenge, risk-taking and perseverance so that children learn to embrace both success and failure as part of the learning process.
We want every child to fulfil their potential, not only academically but as a valued member of the wider community. We support pupils to develop the knowledge, skills and character needed to contribute positively to the world around them.
We value the partnership between home and school and work closely with parents to ensure that every child is happy, safe and successful.

pageCache.pageTitle: British Values - Hook Lane Primary School
pageCache.text:
British Values
text
The DfE have stated that schools should actively promote “the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.”
As a result of the promotion of British values, pupils at Hook Lane are expected to develop:
An understanding of how citizens can influence decision-making through the democratic process;
An appreciation that living under the rule of law protects individual citizens and is essential for their wellbeing and safety;
An understanding that there is a separation of power between the executive and the judiciary, and that whilst some public bodies such as the police and the army can be held to account through Parliament, others such as the courts maintain independence;
An understanding that the freedom to choose and hold other faiths and beliefs is protected in law;
An acceptance that other people having different faiths and beliefs to oneself (or having none) should be accepted and tolerated, and should not be the cause of prejudicial or discriminatory behaviour.
An understanding of the importance of identifying and combatting discrimination.
At Hook Lane, British Values are promoted through a variety of channels, such as:
Teaching within the curriculum
Planned assembly themes
The promotion of our school Vision and Ethos
The implementation of our school behaviour policy and inclusion policy
Use of rewards and sanctions
Extended curriculum e.g. trips, visitors and themed weeks
Responsibilities such as games gang, peer support etc.
Celebration of work through displays, website, assembly
Provision of time for reflection and debate e.g. philosophy, circle-time
This list is not exhaustive.
For more information, view Dfe Guidance for Promoting Fundamental British Values through SMSC

7.45am to 8.45am (Term time only)

pageCache.pageTitle: Meet our People - Hook Lane Primary School

Meet our People
text
The best way to understand what it is like to work at Hook Lane Primary School is to hear from the people who do it every day.
Our staff come from a range of backgrounds and career stages, united by a shared commitment to helping children thrive.
Many colleagues have chosen to build long careers at Hook Lane, while others have joined more recently and brought fresh ideas and experiences to our school community.
If you're considering joining us, we hope their stories will give you a genuine insight into life at Hook Lane.
Real Staff Stories
While every experience is unique, colleagues consistently highlight the importance of strong relationships, supportive teams and the opportunity to make a meaningful difference.
Here's what some of our staff say about working at Hook Lane:
“I love that Hook Lane is a warm, friendly, community-focused place to work that benefits from Trust level communication and collaboration while retaining its own ethos and identity.”
“Working for the school is amazing. We are all like a family and there is always lots of support with school issues and personal issues—you can always get advice and support.”
“The people, the children, the day to day activities and life. The amazing feeling of belonging and doing something different every day to help children develop and become ready for life.”
“The staff are brilliant and we genuinely all get along so well. We laugh often and support each other greatly.”

The Difference Our People Make
Every colleague brings something unique to Hook Lane, whether they're supporting learning in the classroom, leading a project, helping families, running enrichment activities or contributing to the wider life of the school.
Together, our staff create the welcoming, inclusive and ambitious environment that children and families value so highly.
It's this collective commitment, care and teamwork that makes Hook Lane such a special place to learn and work.
Take the Next Step in Your Journey
If the stories on this page have resonated with you, we'd love to hear from you.
At Hook Lane Primary School, you'll join a team where people support one another, contribute ideas and work together to help every child thrive.

pageCache.pageTitle: Naomie Mote - Hook Lane Primary School
pageCache.text:
Naomie Mote
From law student to future teacher: Naomie Mote’s journey through education at Hook Lane
For Naomi, a career in education wasn't always part of the plan.
Before joining Hook Lane seven years ago, she was studying Law at university and had ambitions of pursuing a legal career. But after becoming a parent at 21, Naomi began to reassess what she wanted from her future.
"I remember thinking, 'I can't go into law right now,'" she says. "I started thinking about what I could do while raising my child, and education felt like the right path."
That decision led Naomi to complete an Early Years Professional qualification and eventually apply for a Teaching Assistant role at Hook Lane, the first school she had ever worked in.
"When a TA role came up at Hook Lane, I applied, got the job, and the rest is history," she says.
Over the past seven years, Naomi has progressed from Teaching Assistant to Higher Level Teaching Assistant (HLTA), a role she has held for the last three years. Today, she plans and delivers lessons, covers classes and supports pupils across the school, all while continuing to develop her own skills and experience.
For Naomi, one of the most rewarding aspects of being an HLTA is the variety the role offers.
"Essentially, I do the role of a Teaching Assistant but with the added responsibility of being able to cover a class," she says. "At Hook Lane, we also plan our own lessons."
Much of Naomi's class cover takes place during teachers' PPA time, where she teaches subjects including Art, Design and Technology, and French, which she has taught since her time as a Teaching Assistant.
"French is my first language and English is my second language," she explains.
Her bilingual background has helped shape both her teaching practice and her understanding of children who may be finding school daunting.
"I was an EAL learner when I started school," she says. "I remember school being really scary because I didn't understand anyone and they couldn't understand me."
"Because of that experience, I really understand what some of our EAL children might be feeling. I always try to take time with those children because I understand that experience personally."
Naomi believes that helping children build confidence is one of the most important parts of working in education.
"I love planning a lesson, delivering it and then seeing those lightbulb moments from the children," she says.
"With Art and DT especially, I'll show them the finished product and they'll often say, 'Miss, I can't do that.' Then we go through the learning journey together, and at the end they're so proud of what they've achieved."
"I want to be the teacher that a child looks back on and thinks, 'She believed in me.'"
Hook Lane has played a significant role in helping Naomi develop professionally, providing opportunities to grow and learn from colleagues around her.
"Before I completed my HLTA training, I had to plan a term's worth of Art for a Year 2 class," she says. "I was definitely thrown in at the deep end, but I actually thrive on that."
She credits much of her development to the support of her colleagues.
"I was lucky enough to work alongside an HLTA who had been in the role for 20 years, and she really took me under her wing and taught me so much."
That culture of support is one of the reasons Naomi believes Hook Lane is such a special place to work.
"The adults around the children are connected and support each other," she says. "There's a real sense that everyone is working together to help children succeed."
As a parent herself, Naomi also values the balance that working in education has given her.
"My daughter is 14 now, and I love that we're off at the same time," she says. "Teaching and education are hard work, but the balance makes a lot of sense when you're a parent."
Looking ahead, Naomi has clear ambitions for the future.
"I'd love to become a teacher," she says. "Being an HLTA has given me incredible foundations to eventually have my own class."
For Naomi, however, becoming a teacher isn't about titles or status. It's about making a lasting difference.
"Ultimately, I want to create a classroom where children feel supported, understood and confident," she says. "If I can be that person for even one child during my teaching career, I'll feel like I've done a good job."

Hook Lane Primary School is proud to be part of Maritime Academy Trust — a family of schools working together to improve life chances for children and create meaningful career opportunities for the people who work within them.
Being part of the Trust means you are supported not only within your school, but across a wider network of colleagues, expertise and professional development opportunities that help you grow in your career.

As part of Hook Lane and Maritime Academy Trust, you will benefit from a wider network designed to support your development, confidence and career progression.
This means your development and opportunities extend beyond a single school, giving you access to wider roles, experience and progression across the Trust.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our SEND Offer - Hook Lane Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our SEND Offer
text
All children are valued, respected and welcomed to the school whatever their additional educational need. We aim for a curriculum where learning activities can be undertaken at a variety of levels and in a variety of different ways that are tailored to meet the individual needs of the child. Our school is on one level and is fully accessible by wheelchair with designated toilets with disabled access.
We will support a child with their learning and development, and ensure that they are fully included in all school activities, whilst helping them to appreciate and build on their individual strengths and social independence.
We make every effort to identify, assess, support and review pupils' special educational needs in line with the SEN Code of Practice and target early intervention to maximise and unlock their potential at the earliest opportunity. We make full use of externally provided facilities and support services where appropriate and regularly signpost parents to local services and work with them to identify the next steps for their child.
Pupils with recognised needs are supported across the curriculum by a team of Teaching Assistants; either within the classroom 1:1 or in small groups, or through attending Intervention Groups outside of the classroom.
expanders
Intervention Groups
Quality first teaching within classrooms and in class support where available is always the first strand of support for your child.
We are able to offer some Intervention support outside of the classroom depending on staff availability and group sizes. These are run on a termly basis to offer additional support for children where concerns have been raised, either by a member of staff or parents. Each child on an Intervention is regularly assessed so that their progress can be measured, and so that they can be removed from the Intervention in a timely fashion.
Some Interventions such as Speech and Language groups are long term programmes and follow set targets and objectives set by a Speech and Language Therapist.
Sensory diets are followed for those children with a recognised condition and a programme set by an Occupational Therapist.
Intervention groups that may be offered to your child include:
Times Tables Rockstars
Reception Narrative programme
Speaking and Listening through Narrative programme
Oral to Written Narrative programme
Memory Magic programme
The Listening programme
Clever Hands programme
Social skills cooking group
ASD diagnosis sharing
Sensory room sessions
Yr6 whole class transition work
MHST (Mental Health Support Team) support for both parents and/or children

Careers & Opportunities
text
Build a Career Where You Can Belong, Grow and Make a Difference
At Hook Lane Primary School, part of Maritime Academy Trust, we believe that education has the power to transform lives—and that starts with the people who work in our school.
We are a warm, welcoming and inclusive school community where every voice is valued and every contribution matters. Many of our colleagues have been part of the Hook Lane family for years, reflecting the strong sense of belonging, shared purpose and commitment that make our school such a special place to work.
Whether you are beginning your career in education, looking for your next challenge, or considering a move into a new role, you will find a school where you are encouraged to contribute ideas, develop your strengths and make a meaningful difference every day.
At Hook Lane, we believe that everyone has a role to play in helping children thrive. Our high challenge, low threat ethos creates an environment where staff feel trusted to innovate, supported to grow, and confident to take the next step in their professional journey.
As part of Maritime Academy Trust, you will also benefit from wider opportunities for professional development, collaboration and career progression, while remaining part of the close-knit school community that makes Hook Lane unique.

Life at our School
What it feels like to work here
What it feels like to work here
Working at Hook Lane Primary School means being part of a school where relationships matter, community is at the heart of everything we do, and no one is expected to succeed alone.
From the moment you arrive, you'll notice the warm welcome, strong teamwork and genuine sense of belonging that run throughout the school. Many of our colleagues have worked here for years, creating a culture built on trust, continuity and shared purpose.
Every day brings something different. You might be delivering engaging lessons, supporting children to overcome challenges, collaborating with colleagues to improve practice, or helping to create the rich enrichment experiences that make Hook Lane such a vibrant place to learn and work.
Whether it's Forest School, OPAL play, community partnerships, educational visits or celebrating children's achievements, staff play an active role in shaping the opportunities that help every child thrive.
For many colleagues, Hook Lane is a place where strong relationships and shared purpose make everyday school life both rewarding and sustainable.
What You Can Expect
A welcoming and inclusive school community where everyone is valued
Children who are enthusiastic, curious and eager to learn
Leaders who are visible, approachable and responsive
A high challenge, low threat culture that encourages creativity and professional growth
Opportunities to contribute to enrichment, community projects and wider school life
A calm, positive environment where success is celebrated and wellbeing matters
Strong teamwork and colleagues who support one another
Supporting Our People
Staff Wellbeing & Support
At Hook Lane, wellbeing is part of everyday school life.
We know that people do their best work when they feel supported, respected and able to be themselves. That's why we've created a culture where colleagues work together, communicate openly and look out for one another.
A supportive team culture where colleagues genuinely help one another
Open communication and approachable leadership
Shared responsibility and collaborative problem-solving
A welcoming environment where everyone feels respected and included
Access to wellbeing resources and support through Maritime Academy Trust
To learn more about staff benefits and wellbeing support across the Trust, visit our dedicated page.
Staff Benefits and Wellbeing
Professional Development & Growth
At Hook Lane, we believe that professional growth comes from being trusted to contribute, encouraged to share ideas and supported to take on new opportunities.
Our high challenge, low threat culture gives colleagues the confidence to develop their skills, explore new approaches and play an active role in shaping school improvement.
Coaching, mentoring and support from experienced colleagues and leaders
Opportunities to collaborate and learn from others across the school
Involvement in school development and improvement initiatives
Opportunities to develop leadership skills at every stage of your career
Access to Trust-wide training, networks and professional development opportunities
Whether you are new to education or preparing for your next career step, you'll be supported to build confidence, develop your expertise and achieve your professional goals.
To learn more about staff benefits and wellbeing support across the Trust, visit our dedicated page.

pageCache.pageTitle: Attendance & Holidays - Hook Lane Primary School
pageCache.text:
Attendance & Holidays
text
Attendance
To enable all pupils to benefit from their education the Hook Lane Governors are committed to securing full attendance at the school and good time keeping on arrival.
Good attendance at school makes it easier for your child to make, and keep, good friends as well as being able to learn well. There is a direct correlation between good school attendance and getting good qualifications at GCSE. The government's expected attendance for primary aged pupils is at least 96%, which allows for the usual incidence of childhood illnesses.
The school encourages and celebrates good attendance through a range of rewards, both for individuals and classes.
We have a structured approach to supporting children with poor attendance and work closely with the Educational Welfare Officer to this end. If your child is too ill to attend school, please ring us on the first morning to let us know. We will pursue any unexplained absence or persistent absence for which there is no authorisation.
Holidays
Holidays taken in school time are not authorised and could result in a fine. Families taking holidays in term time will be referred to the Educational Welfare Officer.

pageCache.pageTitle: Helping Your Child at Home - Hook Lane Primary School
pageCache.text:
Helping Your Child at Home
text
Helping your child at home can have a huge impact on your child’s ability to understand, retain and develop their learning at school. At Hook Lane, we not only ensure that homework is set on a weekly basis, but we also encourage our children to read regularly and use online learning sites for 15 minutes each day.
We believe that parents and carers can foster their child’s love of learning by regularly listening to their children reading aloud and by checking in with what their children are learning at school on a daily basis.
Here you will find a number of resources to help you enhance your child’s education in the comfort of home:
expanders
Ready for School
It is important to help children to be as ready for school as possible through the interactions that they have from birth onwards. The following document gives advice about helping children to develop well during their earliest and most formative years.
Born Ready School Ready Bexley Ready
Parent & Carer Strategies Leaflet for Children with SEND
E-Safety
Being online is an integral part of children and young people’s lives. Social media, online games, websites and apps can be accessed through mobile phones, computers, laptops and tablets – all of which form a part of children and young people’s online world.
The internet and online technology provides new opportunities for young people’s learning and growth, but it can also expose them to new types of risks.
Sometimes it isn’t enough to protect children from online harms by simply banning sites or installing firewalls and filters. As such at Hook Lane we encourage our parents and carers to maintain an open and ongoing discussion about online safety at home/as a family/with their children.
If you’d like to find out more on how you can support your child online, please view our suggested guidance below:
NSPCC E-Safety, Supportifng Parents and Carers
Wellbeing
Promoting positive mental health and wellbeing is so important for the emotional, social and physical development of your child.
One of the most important things you can do to ensure that your child remains happy and keen to learn, is to promote positive feelings and emotions at home. Please browse the following resources for tips and tricks on well-being support:
Mentally Healthy Schools
Anna Freud, National Centre for Children and Families

pageCache.pageTitle: Home Visit Programme - Hook Lane Primary School
pageCache.text:
Home Visit Programme
text
It is well recognised that a strong relationship between families and school provides the best possible support for every child. The Education Endowment Foundation is the UK’s leading education research organisation. Their most recent report on parent engagement suggests that effective parent engagement can lead to learning gains of 3 months over the course of a year. This makes effective parent engagement a key element of successfully supporting every child to thrive, our vision for every child in a Maritime school.
We piloted additional home visits in three Maritime schools in September 2022. We received lots of positive feedback from teachers, parents and children and have been running whole school home visits at Hook Lane since then to strengthen the relationship between our school and families.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Approach to Remote Learning - Hook Lane Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our Approach to Remote Learning
text
At Hook Lane, we know that learning works best when school and home work together. If there were ever a need for remote learning, we would use Google Classroom as our main platform to share learning and keep in touch with families. We would take a short amount of time (usually a day or two) to make sure everything was set up and running smoothly before lessons began.
Children’s learning would be delivered in a variety of ways to keep them engaged and supported. This might include:
Using trusted online resources such as Reading Plus, Numbots, Oxford Owls and IXL.
Completing tasks set out clearly on Google Classroom.
Joining virtual lessons with their teacher on Google Meet, where appropriate.
We would aim to keep the curriculum as close as possible to the expectations for each child’s year group or stage of development. Children would be encouraged to engage with their learning each day, and we would keep track so that no child missed out.
Just as importantly, we would make sure children’s wellbeing was looked after. If a child wasn’t regularly joining Google Meets, we would check in at least weekly with a phone call or, if needed, a home visit. Our priority is always to ensure that children feel supported, safe, and ready to learn.
We understand that remote learning can be challenging, and we would work closely with families to provide guidance, reassurance, and practical help wherever it is needed. Together, we can make sure every child continues to thrive.
